episode_title: The Greatest Productivity Mantra: Kaator Re Bhaaji

stories.summary: Abbé Faria, a Goan priest and hypnotist (and character in The Count of Monte Cristo), was once a nervous child giving a sermon to the Queen of Portugal. He froze. His father whispered 'Kaator re bhaaji' (Konkani for 'Just cut the vegetables'). The advice meant: Don't be intimidated by the royalty; treat them like vegetables. Just do your job.
stories.insight: Overcome performance anxiety by trivializing the audience/task. Just do the work.

stories.summary: A ceramics teacher divided a class into two groups. Group A was graded on the *quality* of a single pot. Group B was graded on the *quantity* (weight) of pots produced. The best pots came from Group B. While Group A theorized about perfection, Group B just kept making pots, learning from mistakes.
stories.insight: Quantity leads to quality. Iteration beats planning.

stories.summary: YouTuber Ali Abdaal took 26 weeks and 50 videos to reach 1,000 subscribers. If he had focused on metrics early on, he would have quit. He advises creators to make 2 videos a week for 2 years before even looking at the analytics.
stories.insight: Ignore metrics in the beginning. Focus on the process and the habit.

stories.summary: Donald Knuth, the computer scientist, created the TeX typesetting system. He considers it 'finished' and offers a cash prize to anyone who finds a bug. It is a rare example of software that is mature, stable, and bug-free.
stories.insight: Maturity and stability in tools (like Unix/TeX) are undervalued in a world obsessed with the new.

core_ideas.explanation: Don't let the perfect be the enemy of the good. The first draft is just to 'get it done'. You can't fix a blank page.
Don't focus on the outcome ('I want to read a book'). Focus on the identity ('I am a reader'). If you believe you are a reader, you will read naturally.
Don't praise intelligence (adjective); praise effort (verb). Praising intelligence creates a fixed mindset where people are afraid to fail. Praising effort creates a growth mindset.
Ajay's two superpowers. To last in the long game of life, you need the curiosity to keep learning and the endurance to keep going when things are tough.

jokes_and_cultural_references.content: 'Kaator Re Bhaaji' - Konkani for 'Cut the vegetables'. A mantra for focusing on the task, not the pressure.
Amit jokes that in Marathi, 'Bug' means something else (implying a cuss word or something similar, though he doesn't say it).
'We contain multitudes.' - Walt Whitman (quoted by Amit when contradicting himself).
